learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of mathematics and other basic sciences inherent to their engineering specialty, at a level that allows acquiring the rest of the degree's competencies.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods appropriately, and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Engineering projects: Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems of their specialty, that comply with established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes and their limitations in their field of specialty.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.

Communicates, searches, and structures information correctly orally: Makes a clear and concise oral presentation and defense of the project, adequately using the aspects included in the oral communication guide and computer tools.

syllabus_topics: Oscillations and waves: Simple harmonic motion. Oscillations. Wave motion. Characteristics of waves. Wave phenomena.
Electrostatics: Electric charge. Coulomb's law. Electric field. Electric potential. Electrostatic energy. Capacitors.

Direct current circuits: Electric current. Resistance. Joule effect. Electromotive force. Ohm's law. Electric power. Circuit analysis techniques: Kirchhoff's laws, Thévenin's theorem, superposition principle.
Electromagnetism: Magnetic fields. Field sources. Magnetic flux. Electromagnetic forces. Forces on currents. Magnetic materials. Electromagnetic induction. Inductance.
Alternating current circuits: Analysis of RLC alternating current circuits in steady state. Complex impedance. Phasors. Active, reactive, and apparent power. Power factor.
teaching_methods: Development, writing, and presentation of reports, memos, audiovisual material, etc., related to projects/POPBLs, carried out individually or in teams
Individual study and work, tests, exams, and/or control points
Professor's presentation in the classroom, in participatory classes, of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects
Completion of exercises individually and in teams

assessment_methods.method: Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation delivered, technical presentation and defense
Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices

assessment_rules: For technical competencies evaluated by written and oral tests, the final grade includes a written recovery (75%) and a control point (25%). Practices and self-assessments can be recovered through continuous assessment. For assessments related to technical capacity, project involvement, and project defense, no recovery mechanisms are stated.
